acceptance_criteria.description: MCP listTools exposes exactly one additive tauri_dialog entry with the existing strict bounded dialog schema and a description that states the explicit authorization boundary.

tauri_dialog routes its validated input and AbortSignal through PumarejoDomainPorts.dialog and PumarejoRuntime.dialog; unsupported ports fail with a sanitized integration error, and supplied stale or foreign bindings fail closed.

Contract and runtime tests prove detect, authorized accept/cancel routing, invalid-input rejection, session scoping, and absence of provider identifiers, grants, nonces, paths, and raw causes in public output.
Focused contract/runtime tests and the TypeScript build pass without regressions to the existing public tool set.

closed_decisions: The public API addition is exactly one additive MCP tool named tauri_dialog; existing tools and names remain unchanged.
The tool uses the existing strict dialog input schema and PumarejoRuntime.dialog authorization path; no second authorization path or provider endpoint is introduced.

Detect is observational. Accept and cancel require explicit authorize=true and an effective current surfaceRef/generation binding; omitted binding fields may derive from the active snapshot, while explicitly supplied stale or foreign fields fail closed.
Public results and errors remain bounded and sanitized and must not disclose provider instance identifiers, grants, nonces, paths, or raw causes.

focused: pnpm vitest run tests/contract/mcp-server.test.ts tests/unit/mcp-runtime.test.ts tests/unit/native-control.test.ts

forbidden_changes: Do not edit files outside owned_files.

Do not broaden the dialog schema, change the provider implementation, installer, dependencies, vendored provider, process custody, manifests, lockfiles, queue/blocker/release files, git, Jira, or pull requests.
Do not add implicit authorization, wildcard authorization, dialog polling, arbitrary OS-dialog control, provider endpoint exposure, or reusable grants.
Do not rename, remove, reorder semantically, or weaken validation for existing public MCP tools.
objective: Expose the already implemented launch-scoped native dialog boundary as the additive public MCP tool tauri_dialog without weakening authorization, freshness, or sanitization guarantees.
